pointers.sentence: The documentation gives its purpose: to make the docstrings of the installed applications' models, views, tags and filters readable from the admin (`docs/ref/contrib/admin/admindocs.txt`).

The admin's base template reverses `"django-admindocs-docroot"` with `{% url … as docsroot %}`, which leaves the variable empty when the name does not exist, and shows active staff a link "Documentation" when it does (`django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/base.html`).
The URLconf `django.contrib.admindocs.urls` has no application namespace (`django/contrib/admindocs/urls.py`).

Then it reads `docutils_is_available`, set as `django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py` is imported by trying to import docutils: without docutils, every page renders `"admin_doc/missing_docutils.html"` in place of its own.

`BaseAdminDocsView.get_context_data` adds the default site's `AdminSite.each_context`, for the admin's titles and navigation (`django/contrib/admindocs/views.py:BaseAdminDocsView`, `django/contrib/admin/views/decorators.py:staff_member_required`).

`BaseAdminDocsView.get_context_data` adds the default site's `AdminSite.each_context`, for the admin's titles and navigation (`django/contrib/admindocs/views.py:BaseAdminDocsView`, `django/contrib/admin/views/decorators.py:staff_member_required`).

They take `Engine.template_builtins`, then `Engine.template_libraries` sorted by name ([Libraries: `Library`, custom tags and `{% load %}`](../templates/libraries.md)), and parse the docstring of each function in a library's `Library.tags` or `Library.filters` (`django/contrib/admindocs/views.py:TemplateTagIndexView.get_context_data`).

It reads no docstring, and names each view by `get_view_name`: a view made by `View.as_view` by its class, any other callable by its module and qualified name, or its class's name when it has none (`django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py:get_view_name`).

A model admin's view is a wrapper that takes the names of the bound method it wraps, and so is named by the class that defines the method: here every change list is `ModelAdmin.changelist_view`, while the user's add page is `UserAdmin.add_view`, an override (`django/contrib/admin/options.py:ModelAdmin.get_urls`).

`ViewDetailView` accepts a view's name from the URL only if it is the `URLPattern.lookup_str` of some pattern; any other is a 404, and nothing is imported for it (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver._is_callback`, `django/contrib/admindocs/views.py:ViewDetailView._get_view_func`).

`ViewDetailView` accepts a view's name from the URL only if it is the `URLPattern.lookup_str` of some pattern; any other is a 404, and nothing is imported for it (`django/urls/resolvers.py:URLResolver._is_callback`, `django/contrib/admindocs/views.py:ViewDetailView._get_view_func`).
`ModelDetailView` answers 404 for an unknown application or model, and raises `PermissionDenied` without the permission (`django/contrib/admindocs/views.py:user_has_model_view_permission`).
A model's page is built from `_meta` (`django/contrib/admindocs/views.py:ModelDetailView.get_context_data`).

The methods are the functions, properties and cached properties in the model class's own `__dict__`, less names beginning with a prefix of `MODEL_METHODS_EXCLUDE`: a property, a `cached_property` or a method that takes only `self` is shown as a field, typed by `get_return_data_type` from its name, and any other under "Methods with arguments" ([Asking a callable what it accepts: `django/utils/inspect.py`](../utils/inspect.md)).

It takes the default engine's `Engine.dirs`, then the directories of each loader that has a `get_dirs` method, each once, joins the template's name onto each with `safe_join`, and says whether each file exists (`django/contrib/admindocs/views.py:TemplateDetailView.get_context_data`).

It splits a docstring at blank lines: the first part is the title; the last, if it parses as email headers (`"Context: port, berths"`), is the metadata, of which a view's page shows `"Context"` and `"Templates"`; the rest is the body (`django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py:parse_docstring`).

It wraps the text in directives that make `"cmsreference"` the default role, so that text in single backquotes links in the context the caller names, `"model"`, `"view"`, `"tag"` or `"filter"`; it bases the roles' links on the reversed `"django-admindocs-docroot"`, and turns off raw HTML and the inclusion of files (`django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py:parse_rst`).

The roles are registered with docutils as the module is imported, if docutils is there: `default_reference_role` as `"cmsreference"`, and one for each entry of `ROLES` by `create_reference_role`, which lowercases a target but a view's or a template's, names the comment says are case-sensitive (`django/contrib/admindocs/utils.py:create_reference_role`).

For a `"HEAD"` request from an address in `INTERNAL_IPS`, or from a user who is active and staff, it returns an empty response with the header X-View, the view's name by `get_view_name`, and the view is never called ([The centre of the chain](../handlers/view.md)); any other request passes (`django/contrib/admindocs/middleware.py:XViewMiddleware.process_view`).

The bookmarklets page's link of JavaScript sends a `"HEAD"` request for the page the browser is on and opens the page of the view X-View names (`django/contrib/admindocs/templates/admin_doc/bookmarklets.html`).
Most of Django's middleware set `async_capable = False`; not `XViewMiddleware`, which, the release notes say, implements neither `process_request` nor `process_response` (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`).
